promptText: Which hotel brands are commonly considered when an owner wants to affiliate an independent upper-upscale property through a conversion in the Caribbean and Latin America?

payload.rawResponseText:
This is a great question that sits at the intersection of hotel development strategy and brand management. Based on the latest industry data, here is a comprehensive overview of the hotel brands most commonly considered when an independent owner wants to affiliate an upper-upscale property through a conversion in the **Caribbean and Latin America (CALA)**:

---

## 🏨 Key Hotel Brands for Upper-Upscale Conversions in the Caribbean & Latin America

### 1. 🔵 **Marriott International** — Multiple Conversion-Friendly Brands


Hotel conversions have real momentum in the Caribbean and Latin America (CALA) region and in recent years have become an important growth driver for Marriott International.
 
The company has continued to see strong momentum in the space thanks to its broad array of conversion-friendly brands across different segments, including **The Luxury Collection, Autograph Collection Hotels, Tribute Portfolio, Delta Hotels, and Four Points by Sheraton**. In the Caribbean and Latin America, more than 50 percent of Marriott's room signings were conversions in a recent year.


Key upper-upscale brands within Marriott's conversion toolkit include:

- **Autograph Collection Hotels**: 
Autograph Collection is a group of independent upper-upscale to luxury hotels within the Marriott International portfolio.
 
The Caribbean and Central America alone account for 26 Autograph Collection sites.
 A recent example: 
the Royalton Riviera Cancun converted into Marriott's Autograph Collection, as part of Blue Diamond Resorts' affiliation with Marriott Bonvoy.


- **The Luxury Collection**: 
The Dominican Republic is home to the Sanctuary Cap Cana, a Luxury Collection Adult All-Inclusive Resort, which rebranded in September 2022 — it was the first All-Inclusive by Marriott property in the luxury segment.


- **Westin**: 
The Westin Porto de Galinhas, an All-Inclusive Resort in Brazil, opened after an extensive renovation — a conversion effort in collaboration with PGA Hotel Management Group that brought the Westin brand and Marriott's first All-Inclusive resort to Brazil.


- **Tribute Portfolio**: Also listed among Marriott's conversion-friendly options, it targets independent-spirited upper-upscale hotels seeking soft brand affiliation.

---

### 2. 🟡 **Hilton** — Curio Collection & Tapestry Collection


Hilton has more than 150 hotels in the pipeline for CALA, including a combination of both new developments and conversion projects, giving Hilton the opportunity to expand its brand presence in a variety of market segments.


- **Curio Collection by Hilton**: 
One of the standout aspects of Hilton's expansion in the region has been its remarkable growth in luxury and lifestyle brands, with the **Conrad Hotels & Resorts, Curio Collection by Hilton**, and Waldorf Astoria brands among those that have seen significant growth in the region.


- **Tapestry Collection by Hilton**: 
The Curio and Tapestry Collections by Hilton are the company's upper-upscale collections.
 
Hilton has also focused on expanding its lifestyle offerings with brands like Canopy by Hilton and Tapestry Collection by Hilton, designed to cater to younger, more adventurous travelers looking for unique and immersive stays.


---

### 3. 🟢 **IHG Hotels & Resorts** — Vignette Collection, voco & Kimpton


IHG's soft-brand and conversion-friendly brands have helped to drive growth in the region. It signed two **Vignette Collection** properties in CALA in a recent year along with opening one in Peru.


- **Vignette Collection**: 
SOUMA Hotel Lima became the first South American Vignette Collection hotel, opening in March 2025 with minimalist design and décor inspired by Peru's Pacaya Samiria Nature Reserve.
 This IHG soft brand is particularly suited to independent upper-upscale hotels that want to retain their identity.

- **voco Hotels**: 
Reopened in late 2024 after a thorough conversion, voco Hermosillo serves as a vibrant reentry of the premium voco brand into a key Mexican city.


- **Kimpton Hotels**: 
2024 openings included the Kimpton Mas Olas Resort and Spa in Baja California, Mexico. Many of these will offer branded residences beyond guest rooms and suites, including a forthcoming joint Kimpton hotel and residence offering in Tulum, Mexico.


- 
IHG Hotels & Resorts has about 300 hotels open in the Caribbean and Latin America region with another 100 in the pipeline.


---

### 4. 🔴 **Choice Hotels International** — Radisson Blu, Radisson Individuals & Ascend Collection


Choice Hotels relaunched **Radisson Individuals** as an upper-upscale soft brand focused on full-service, boutique and independent hotels that stand apart for their distinctive local character and superior guest service.
 
Choice is extending the brand to owners, marking another step in the company's expansion in the upper-upscale tier at a time of rising consumer demand in this space.


- **Radisson Blu**: 
In 2025, Choice Hotels is opening an 80-room, full-service Radisson Blu in Bariloche, Argentina.


- **Radisson Individuals**: 
In May 2025, it opened the V Grand Hotel, a member of Radisson Individuals in Medellin, Colombia.


- **Ascend Hotel Collection**: 
Choice Hotels also plans to introduce an Ascend Collection hotel in Calama, Chile.
 This soft brand is also a conversion-friendly upper-upscale option.

---

### 5. 🟣 **Hyatt** — The Unbound Collection, Destination by Hyatt & Unscripted by Hyatt

- **The Unbound Collection by Hyatt**: 
Hyatt's soft brands are providing growth opportunities overseas. Destination by Hyatt, made up of 17 upper-upscale and luxury resorts, has a few new properties coming online overseas.


- **Unscripted by Hyatt** (newest): 
Hyatt launched Unscripted, a new soft brand targeting upscale independent hotels that want to retain their unique identity while leveraging Hyatt's marketing and loyalty programs. Around 40 hotels worldwide are in talks to join, mostly through converting existing independent properties rather than new construction.
 
The brand gives independent properties and small portfolios a light-touch operating model and flexible brand standards — empowering owners to maintain their unique identity and positioning while benefiting from Hyatt's scale.


---

### 6. 🟠 **Accor** — MGallery, Emblems Collection & Sofitel


Thomas Dubaere, CEO of the Americas for premium, midscale and economy brands at Accor, noted opportunities for unused space to convert into hotels in Latin America.
 Accor's upper-upscale conversion-friendly brands in CALA include **MGallery** (a soft brand for boutique upper-upscale properties), **Sofitel**, and the **Emblems Collection** — all of which allow independent properties to retain much of their character while gaining access to ALL - Accor Live Limitless loyalty program.

---

### 7. ⚪ **Wyndham Hotels & Resorts** — Trademark Collection & Registry Collection


New conversion hotels in the Caribbean include properties converting to **Trademark Collection by Wyndham**. The Buccaneer Beach & Golf Resort in St. Croix is an upscale property converting to Wyndham's Trademark Collection, marking the first Wyndham Hotels & Resorts property in St. Croix.
 For higher-end independent properties, Wyndham's **Registry Collection Hotels** is its upper-upscale/luxury soft brand option.

---

## 📌 Summary Table

| Brand Family | Upper-Upscale Conversion Brands in CALA |
|---|---|
| **Marriott** | Autograph Collection, Tribute Portfolio, The Luxury Collection, Westin |
| **Hilton** | Curio Collection, Tapestry Collection, Canopy by Hilton |
| **IHG** | Vignette Collection, voco, Kimpton |
| **Choice / Radisson** | Radisson Individuals, Radisson Blu, Ascend Hotel Collection |
| **Hyatt** | The Unbound Collection, Destination by Hyatt, Unscripted by Hyatt |
| **Accor** | MGallery, Emblems Collection, Sofitel |
| **Wyndham** | Trademark Collection, Registry Collection Hotels |

In general, 
hotels affiliated with international brands used to be few and far between across Latin America, but that's now changing as investor appetite for conversions grows. Post-pandemic, more owners started to understand the importance of branding.
 The trend is clearly accelerating, with all major hotel companies competing aggressively for independent upper-upscale properties throughout the Caribbean and Latin America.
